title: Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism and Kallmann Syndrome: Olfactory and Neuroendocrine Axes

steps.title: Operational Criteria for Delayed Pubertal Onset

vis.alt: Left hand radiograph with a bone age reading marked for each hand bone.
vis.caption: Bone age from a left hand film: one reading per bone. Credit: Mikael Häggström.

steps.tx: Delayed puberty is absence of initial secondary sexual signs by 13 years in girls (no breast buds) or 14 years in boys (testicular volume < 4 mL), or absence of menarche by 15-16 years. Applying standardized **Delayed puberty operational definitions** highlights that stature velocity frequently wanes during early adolescence due to missing pubertal growth spurts. Systematic auxological monitoring distinguishes isolated pubertal delay from broader chronic systemic or neuroendocrine diseases.
steps.say: Pubertal onset is formally delayed when secondary sexual characteristics are absent by age thirteen in girls or age fourteen in boys.

steps.title: Biochemical Profile of Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism

vis.alt: Hypothalamic GnRH driving pituitary gonadotropins and gonadal steroids at puberty.
vis.caption: The HPG axis: GnRH, gonadotropins and gonadal steroids. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Characterized by inappropriately low or undetectable serum LH and FSH in the presence of subnormal sex steroids (testosterone < 20 ng/dL in boys, estradiol < 10 pg/mL in girls). Verifying the **Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism biochemical profile** distinguishes it from hypergonadotropic states where gonadotropins rise markedly. Conversely, hypogonadotropic profiles establish failure of the hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone pulse generator or anterior pituitary gonadotrophs.
steps.say: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism demonstrates low or undetectable gonadotropins alongside subnormal testosterone or estradiol levels.

steps.title: Embryological Defect in Kallmann Syndrome

nodes.label:
Disrupted Co-Migration
Axons fail to reach cribriform plate

Hypothalamic Arrest
GnRH neurons fail to reach arcuate nucleus

Kallmann Phenotype
Anosmia plus hypogonadotropic hypogonadism

steps.tx: Kallmann syndrome pairs congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia or hyposmia due to defective embryonic co-migration of GnRH neuroendocrine cells and olfactory axons from the olfactory placode. Understanding **Kallmann syndrome anosmia and embryology** explains how GnRH neuroblasts migrate along olfactory and vomeronasal nerves across the cribriform plate into the hypothalamus. Failure of axonal elongation leads to agenesis of olfactory bulbs.
steps.say: Kallmann syndrome links hypogonadism with anosmia due to disrupted embryonic co-migration of GnRH neurons and olfactory nerves.

steps.title: Genetics of Syndromic Kallmann Variants

left.title: X-Linked Form (ANOS1 / KAL1)
points: Unilateral renal agenesis in 30% of affected boys

right.title: Autosomal Dominant / Recessive
points: FGFR1 mutations with cleft lip and dental agenesis
PROKR2 and PROK2 prokineticin signaling defects
CHD7 mutations overlapping with CHARGE syndrome

steps.tx: X-linked Kallmann is caused by ANOS1 / KAL1 mutations (Xp22.3, paired with bimanual synkinesia and unilateral renal agenesis); autosomal forms involve FGFR1, PROKR2, and CHD7. Mapping **Kallmann genetic variants (ANOS1, FGFR1, PROKR2)** demonstrates how anosmin-1 guides axonal pathfinding during cranial morphogenesis. Identifying associated features like involuntary mirror hand movements or absent kidney focuses targeted genetic testing and renal ultrasonography.
steps.say: X-linked Kallmann syndrome from ANOS1 mutations features involuntary mirror hand movements and unilateral renal agenesis alongside anosmia.

steps.title: Normosmic Idiopathic Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism

rows: Failure of arcuate KNDy pulse generation
Loss of upstream GnRH release trigger

steps.tx: Patients with nIHH have completely intact sense of smell, harboring mutations in GNRHR, TAC3 / TACR3 (neurokinin B pathway), KISS1 / KISS1R (kisspeptin pathway), or GNRH1. Evaluating **Normosmic idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (nIHH)** via formal smell testing with the University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test reliably distinguishes nIHH from Kallmann. Defective kisspeptin-neurokinin signaling impairs pulsatile GnRH release despite anatomically normal hypothalamic development.
steps.say: Normosmic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism retains normal olfactory function and stems from defects in kisspeptin or neurokinin signaling pathways.

steps.title: Diagnostic Window of Infantile Mini-Puberty

nodes.label:
Placental Steroid Clearance
Postnatal withdrawal of estrogens

Pituitary Surge
LH and FSH peak at 1-3 months

Mini-Puberty Window
Testosterone peaks at 1-6 months

Diagnostic Seam
Absent surge detects hypogonadism early

steps.tx: During the neonatal mini-puberty (1-6 months of life), normal infants exhibit transient activation of LH/FSH and testosterone/estradiol; absence of mini-puberty in an infant boy with cryptorchidism and micropenis identifies congenital hypogonadism. Leveraging the **Mini-puberty window for early infant diagnosis** allows measuring serum gonadotropins and testosterone to circumvent waiting until 14 years of age. Inhibin B and AMH provide supplemental markers of Sertoli cell mass.
steps.say: The infant mini-puberty window permits early diagnosis of congenital hypogonadism in baby boys presenting with micropenis and undescended testes.

steps.title: Testosterone Escalation Regimen in Adolescent Boys

nodes.label:
Initial Low-Dose Depot
Testosterone enanthate 50 mg IM monthly

Stepwise Escalation
Increase by 50 mg every 6 months

Gradual Virilization
Phallic growth, voice, height spurt

Full Adult Replacement
200 mg IM every 2 weeks

steps.tx: Pubertal induction begins with low-dose depot testosterone (testosterone enanthate 50 mg IM monthly for 6 months, escalating by 50 mg every 6 months to adult dose 200 mg every 2 weeks). A structured **Pubertal induction regimen in adolescent boys** mirrors normal physiological puberty, allowing proportionate skeletal trunk growth and avoiding premature epiphyseal arrest. Serial bone age radiographs guide dose advancement toward adult replacement levels.
steps.say: Pubertal induction in adolescent boys uses gradually escalating depot testosterone over two to three years to mimic normal pubertal development.

steps.title: Gonadotropin Therapy for Future Fertility Induction

left.title: Testosterone Monotherapy
points: Does not stimulate spermatogenesis or testicular growth

right.title: Pulsatile / Gonadotropin Protocol
points: hCG (1000-2000 IU twice weekly) stimulates Leydig cells
Achieves testicular enlargement and fertile sperm counts

steps.tx: Unlike testosterone replacement which does not stimulate spermatogenesis, gonadotropin therapy combining human chorionic gonadotropin hCG (LH analog, 1000-2000 IU twice weekly) with recombinant FSH follitropin induces testicular growth and fertile spermatogenesis. Utilizing **Gonadotropin therapy for future fertility** primes immature Sertoli cells with recombinant follitropin before human chorionic gonadotropin stimulates Leydig cells to produce high local intratesticular testosterone. Successful spermatogenesis is achieved in up to 80-90% of hypogonadotropic men.
steps.say: Combined human chorionic gonadotropin and follicle-stimulating hormone therapy induces testicular enlargement and fertile sperm production.
